AccessChargeLine.description:
One ACCESS / platform-fee line on a bill (product-scoped or tenant-wide).

⭐ A line is ALWAYS present and its amount MAY BE $0. When no
``tenant_access_charge`` row matches, the generator emits an explicit zero
line rather than an empty array, so the itemisation agrees with the
``access_charge_usd`` aggregate it summarises. An absent row cannot be
audited or reconciled; a $0.00 row can.
AccessChargeLine.title: AccessChargeLine

ActorCostLine.description:
One ACTING person's spend in a tenant over the window (billing_cost_actor_daily).

``actor_id`` is WHO ACTED (the Keycloak sub); ``subject_id`` is WHO PAID (the licences Subject).
``actor_id = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000005`` is spend no person initiated.
Split by ``byo`` because a BYO line's cost is the customer's own provider bill, not the platform's.
ActorCostLine.title: ActorCostLine

AttributionRulePut.description:
Upsert one ``billing_attribution_rules`` row, keyed on its match tuple.

Match tuple: ``(source_tenant_id, source_subject_id, match_project)``.
``source_subject_id`` omitted = any subject under the source tenant.
``actor_id`` omitted = re-tenant only, keep whatever actor arrived.
AttributionRulePut.title: AttributionRulePut

BillingTotals.description:
The tenant-month rollup, as ``services.billing.generate_billing`` emits it.

⛔ EVERY KEY THE GENERATOR PUTS IN ``totals`` MUST BE DECLARED HERE, for the
``extra='ignore'`` reason ``LicenseCostBilling`` spells out above.

⭐ THE SEAT AXIS IS WHY THIS ONE MATTERED MOST. ``seat_fee_usd`` is in
``services.invoices._TOTAL_COMPONENT_COLUMNS`` and the generator's own comment
calls the seat axis *"disjoint from access_charge_usd above, and both are
components of total_usd"*. Undeclared, a caller reconciling
``customer_cost_usd`` off this response was short by the ENTIRE seat fee with
nothing in the payload naming the gap — the same shape alembic ``0033`` fixed
on the invoice side when the app-request stream was missing from
``InvoiceDocument``.

Every field added here carries a default so no existing construction site
changes shape; the generator emits all of them on every call.
BillingTotals.title: BillingTotals

BudgetAggregateStatus.description: Tenant-level aggregate across all currently-active stacked budgets.
BudgetAggregateStatus.title: BudgetAggregateStatus

BudgetReserveRequest.description:
Pre-flight reservation against a tenant's budget pool.

license-authz calls this on the request hot path to atomically check
that the tenant has enough budget headroom for the request and reserve
the tokens for a short window (TTL). The reservation auto-expires; the
actual cost is debited post-fact via the cost-event flush, so a
reservation that doesn't end up incurring the full estimated cost
self-corrects within ``ttl_seconds``.

license_id.description: Optional license scope. If unset, all active budgets for the tenant are pooled.
license_id.title: License Id

ttl_seconds.description: How long the reservation is held before auto-expiring (clamped 5-600s).
ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds

BudgetReserveRequest.title: BudgetReserveRequest

BudgetReserveResponse.description: Result of a budget reservation attempt.

cap_tokens.description: Sum of cap (budget_tokens) across the active budget pool.
cap_tokens.title: Cap Tokens

in_flight_reserved_tokens.description: Sum of currently-held reservations (this one + others).
in_flight_reserved_tokens.title: In Flight Reserved Tokens

reason.description: When allowed=False, machine-readable reason: 'over_budget' | 'no_active_budget' | 'redis_unavailable' | 'tenant_archived'. ⚠️ 'tenant_archived' is the only one that is an AUTHORISATION verdict rather than an accounting one, and it is the only one a caller must treat as terminal: retrying with a smaller estimate cannot help. It is raised in routers/budget.py BEFORE reserve_budget runs, because an archived tenant with no budget row would otherwise be ALLOWED by 'no_active_budget'. ⛔ The other three are bare string literals constructed in services/budget_redis.py and nothing enforces agreement with this list or with metrics.BUDGET_RESERVE_REFUSAL_REASONS -- a new reason must be added in all three places.
reason.title: Reason

remaining_tokens.description: Headroom *after* this reservation. Caller can decide whether to retry shortly.
remaining_tokens.title: Remaining Tokens

reservation_id.description: Opaque per-reservation handle minted on success, in BOTH settlement modes. ⭐ CORRECTED: this used to read 'NULL while BUDGET_REQUIRE_RESERVATION_HANDLE is off', which was the measure-before-arming deadlock — the handle could not be observed end-to-end until the flag that changes settlement was already armed. A handle is now minted and recorded on every ADMITTED reserve; the flag selects only whether a settlement drains by identity or by anonymous pool. NULL on deny (nothing was held, so there is nothing to discharge) and NULL if the hold could not be recorded — a non-NULL value attests that a hold EXISTS, never that one was intended. Pass it back at settlement (on the cost event's `reservation_id`) so a release drains only this reservation. It is the canonical dashed UUID form and MUST be round-tripped verbatim: it is stored in a Postgres `uuid` column and compared byte-for-byte at settlement.
reservation_id.title: Reservation Id

reserved_tokens.description: Tokens actually held by this reservation (== estimated_tokens on success, 0 on deny).
reserved_tokens.title: Reserved Tokens

BudgetReserveResponse.title: BudgetReserveResponse

BudgetResetRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/budget/reset/{tenant_id}`` — an operator reset.

``reason`` is optional and is recorded on every audit row the reset writes.
It is the only human context the trail will ever carry for a write that
hands a tenant back its whole allowance, so a caller that has one should
send it.
BudgetResetRequest.title: BudgetResetRequest

BudgetResetResponse.description:
What a successful reset reports.

``previous_consumed_total`` is summed from ``effective_consumed`` — the same
reader the status endpoint uses — so it equals the spend the operator saw on
screen, not the raw column (which can still hold a stale earlier period).
BudgetResetResponse.title: BudgetResetResponse

CloseInvoiceRequest.description:
Freeze one tenant-month into a persisted statement.

``period_end`` is EXCLUSIVE and both bounds are required rather than derived
from a ``YYYY-MM`` string. The generator takes a month, so a period that is
not exactly one calendar month is refused by the service rather than quietly
widened to the containing month — a statement covering a different span than
the one asked for is worse than an error.

``issue_immediately`` defaults to True. A draft is freely mutable by design,
so a long-lived draft is not a statement; the automated closer wants the
number allocated in the same transaction that froze the figures.
CloseInvoiceRequest.title: CloseInvoiceRequest

CommercialTerm.description:
One term, with the PROVENANCE of its value.

⭐ The provenance is not decoration. A `value` of 20 means something
different when it came from an effective-dated rule an operator wrote than
when it fell back to a code constant nobody decided — and the second case is
what every tenant in this estate was silently on before 2026-09-10. A terms
page that shows only numbers cannot tell an operator which tenants have
actually been priced.

`value` is None when the term does not exist for this tenant. That is NOT
zero: no platform fee configured and a $0.00 platform fee are different
commercial facts, and `source` distinguishes them.
CommercialTerm.title: CommercialTerm

CommercialTermsPut.description:
The COMPLETE commercial terms for one tenant. Every field is required.

⭐ REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CONTRACT. This is a PUT:
it states what the tenant's terms ARE, not which of them to nudge. A
partial body is a PATCH, and a PATCH is precisely the shape that produced
the half-configured tenants this endpoint exists to make impossible — a
caller that may omit the markup can forget the markup, and a forgotten
markup is silent lost revenue rather than a failed request. If a caller
wants to change one term it re-states all four, which is cheap, because it
can read them back from `GET` on the same path first.

`seat_app_key` is the PRODUCT the per-seat rate is counted over — it becomes
the access charge's `service_key` as `seat:<app_key>`, which is the form
:func:`services.seats.seat_scope_for_charge` recognises and turns into a
period-scoped, per-app seat count. A bare app key, never a pre-prefixed one;
see `_seat_app_key_is_not_already_prefixed`.

`markup_service_key` scopes the BYO markup rule to one product, so pricing
CommonPractice's BYO spend does not re-price every other product the tenant
consumes. It is a separate field from `seat_app_key` on purpose: licences'
app key and billing's `service_key` are different namespaces that happen to
agree today, and collapsing them here would bake that coincidence in.

`effective_from` is honoured rather than forced to `now` because both
underlying stores are effective-dated and an operator agreeing terms that
start on the 1st must be able to say so. Omit it and every term starts now.

billing_mode.description: The OUTER gate over every resolved markup rule. 'byo_markup_only' is CommonPractice's mode: a BYO line bills its markup percentage and NOT the provider cost, because the customer already paid the provider.
billing_mode.title: Billing Mode

byo_markup_pct.description: Markup percentage charged on that product's BYO lines.
byo_markup_pct.title: Byo Markup Pct

markup_service_key.description: Product the BYO markup rule is scoped to.
markup_service_key.title: Markup Service Key

platform_fee_usd.description: Flat monthly platform fee. Becomes a tenant-wide cadence='monthly' access charge with NO allowance — usage bills on top.
platform_fee_usd.title: Platform Fee Usd

seat_app_key.description: Product whose ACTIVE LICENCES are counted as seats, e.g. 'commonpractice'. Stored as service_key 'seat:<app_key>'.
seat_app_key.title: Seat App Key

seat_fee_usd.description: Per-seat monthly RATE (not a charge) — multiplied by the seat count.
seat_fee_usd.title: Seat Fee Usd

CommercialTermsPut.title: CommercialTermsPut

CommercialTermsRequest.description:
Overrides for `POST /api/config/tenants/{id}/terms`. Omit = use the default.

Every field is optional on purpose: the common call is an empty body meaning
"put this tenant on the standard rate card", and a provisioning caller that
knows nothing about pricing can make exactly that call.
CommercialTermsRequest.title: CommercialTermsRequest

CommercialTermsView.description:
A tenant's currently-effective commercial terms, each with provenance.

The response of BOTH `PUT` and `GET /tenants/{id}/commercial-terms`, so a
caller never needs a second request to learn what it just wrote.

`changed` names the terms this PUT actually re-dated. It is `[]` on a GET and
`[]` on an idempotent replay — which is the observable difference between
"the terms already said this" and "I re-opened four effective-dated
periods", and is the only way a provisioning caller can tell a retry that did
nothing from a retry that shredded a live tenant's history.
CommercialTermsView.title: CommercialTermsView

CorrelationCostGroup.description:
One grouped slice of cost for a set of correlation ids.

``key`` holds the requested group-by dimensions (e.g.
``{"stage": "narration", "model": "claude-opus-4-8"}``); empty when no
group_by was requested (single all-up total).
CorrelationCostGroup.title: CorrelationCostGroup

CorrelationCostResponse.description:
Priced cost for one or more correlation ids (e.g. w2v run_ids).

Read over raw ``cost_events`` (correlation_id indexed) so cost can be sliced
by the caller's operation — what the per-tenant CostDaily rollup cannot do.
CorrelationCostResponse.title: CorrelationCostResponse

DlqDiscardRequest.description:
Operator request to PERMANENTLY drop specific dead-letter entries.

``confirm`` defaults to **False**: a plain call is a DRY RUN that reports
exactly what *would* be discarded and deletes nothing. The operator must opt
in to the destructive path, the same way ``RepriceRequest.dry_run`` makes an
operator opt in to writing money data.

``reason`` is required and must be non-blank. Once an entry is XDEL'd it is
gone; this string is the only record of *why* it was dropped, and it is
written to the audit log and to every per-entry discard log line.

reason.description: Why these entries are being discarded. Recorded in the audit trail.
reason.title: Reason

DlqDiscardRequest.title: DlqDiscardRequest

DlqDiscardResult.description:
Per-entry outcome of one discard run — counts via ``len()`` of each list.

``examined`` counts the requested ids actually FOUND on the dead stream (an
id already gone is examined 0 times and appears in no list). Every examined
id lands in AT MOST one of ``eligible`` / ``refused``.

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: this said "exactly one", and that is not what the
code does. ``examined`` is incremented before the per-id work (dlq_ops, right
after the XRANGE lookup), and the per-id ``except`` below the XDEL swallows
and ``continue``s — deliberately, so one bad entry cannot abort a batch. An
id that fails there is counted in ``examined`` and lands in NEITHER list, so
``len(eligible) + len(refused) <= examined``, with equality only when nothing
failed. A caller asserting equality turns a single Redis hiccup into a hard
stop on an otherwise-good sweep. ``discarded`` is a
subset of ``eligible`` and is ALWAYS empty on a dry run — so a dry run and a
confirmed run that deleted nothing are distinguishable only by the request,
which is why the audit row records ``confirm``.

``refused`` mirrors ``DlqReplayResult.still_malformed``: ``{"id", "reason"}``
with a low-cardinality reason string.
DlqDiscardResult.title: DlqDiscardResult

DlqEntry.description:
One quarantined cost event as it sits on the dead-letter stream.

``fields`` is the original wire payload with the ``_dlq_*`` bookkeeping keys
(and any leading-underscore internal key) stripped out — i.e. exactly what a
replay would re-inject once the malformed condition is fixed.
DlqEntry.title: DlqEntry

DlqInspectResponse.description:
Page of dead-letter entries. ``has_more`` is set when the fetch hit the
(capped) limit, so the operator knows the stream is larger than one page.
DlqInspectResponse.title: DlqInspectResponse

DlqReattributeRequest.description:
Operator request to re-attribute nil/blank-tenant dead-letter entries (#243).

``tenant_id`` is the tenant the spend is billed to. It must resolve to a
registered, non-nil tenant — checked in
:func:`services.dlq_ops.resolve_reattribute_target` (400 otherwise), not
here, because registration is a live-registry question.

``confirm`` defaults to **False**: a plain call is a DRY RUN that reports
what would be re-attributed and writes nothing. ``reason`` is required and
non-blank; it is stamped onto the re-injected event, the receipt row and the
audit log.

reason.description: Why this spend belongs to tenant_id. Recorded in the receipt and audit trail.
reason.title: Reason

tenant_id.description: Registered, non-nil tenant (uuid or registered name) to bill.
tenant_id.title: Tenant Id

DlqReattributeRequest.title: DlqReattributeRequest

DlqReattributeResult.description:
Per-entry outcome of one re-attribution run.

``tenant_id`` is the CANONICAL target. Every examined id lands in at most one
of ``eligible`` / ``already_processed`` / ``still_malformed`` / ``refused``.
``reattributed`` (re-injected onto ``billing:costs``) is a subset of
``eligible`` and is ALWAYS empty on a dry run. ``deleted_from_dlq`` and
``receipt_failed`` partition ``reattributed``: an entry whose Postgres receipt
could not be committed is billed (marker permanent) but NOT deleted.
DlqReattributeResult.title: DlqReattributeResult

DlqReplayRequest.description:
Operator request to replay specific dead-letter entries by stream id.

``delete_on_success`` defaults to **True**: a successfully re-injected entry
is removed from ``billing:costs:dead`` so a second replay is a no-op and the
stream shrinks as it is drained. Set False to re-inject while leaving the
quarantine record in place (audit / dry-drain).
DlqReplayRequest.title: DlqReplayRequest

DlqReplayResult.description:
Per-entry outcome of one replay run.

An id lands in exactly one of the first three lists (or none, if it was not
found on the stream). ``deleted_from_dlq`` is a subset of ``replayed``. An
entry that STILL fails validation is left on the dead stream and reported in
``still_malformed`` — never re-injected — so a premature replay cannot loop a
malformed event back through the consumer.
DlqReplayResult.title: DlqReplayResult

FxRatePut.description: PUT /api/config/fx-rates: USD -> EUR | CAD. USD needs no row (it is 1).

effective_from.description: Defaults to now. Closes the open row at this instant. The FIRST row must be back-dated to before the earliest money event that can still settle: an event older than the first rate settles with NULL consumption (counted as billing_money_unpriced_events_total{reason="before_first_fx_rate"}).
effective_from.title: Effective From

FxRatePut.title: FxRatePut

InvoiceDocument.description:
The frozen pair, returned verbatim by ``/reproduce``.

Read from ``billing_invoices`` and nothing else — no rollup, no markup rule,
no licences call. If re-rendering a statement needed any mutable table, the
statement would not be a record.

⚠️ MONEY IS A STRING HERE, DELIBERATELY. These are the frozen figures; a
float round-trip is a silent edit to something that must not change. The
service emits ``str(Decimal)`` and this model preserves it rather than
coercing back through a numeric type.

``digest_matches`` recomputes sha256 over ``{snapshot, inputs, money}`` at
read time and compares it to the stored column, so "was this row edited?" is
a boolean a caller can act on rather than a diff of two JSONB documents.
⚠️ It used to cover ``{snapshot, inputs}`` ONLY, which made it blind to an
edited ``total_usd`` — the money columns were stored copies nothing checked.

⛔ EVERY FIELD ``reproduce()`` RETURNS MUST BE DECLARED HERE. This model has
no ``model_config``, so Pydantic v2 defaults to ``extra='ignore'`` and an
undeclared key is dropped SILENTLY at ``routers/billing.py`` — a 200 whose
body is missing the field, with nothing in the logs. That is exactly how the
seven frozen components below reached HTTP as nothing on their first attempt.
InvoiceDocument.title: InvoiceDocument

InvoicePreviewExclusions.description:
Spend that was metered and then deliberately NOT billed.

⛔ THIS CANNOT BE READ OFF THE ROLLUP, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS ITS OWN QUERY.
``excluded_from_billing`` / ``exclusion_reason`` live on
``billing_cost_events`` ONLY; ``services.rollup_engine`` filters those rows
out on the way into ``billing_cost_daily``, so the rollup every other
billing reader consumes is already net of them and has no column that could
say by how much. A preview built from the rollup alone therefore shows a
smaller number than the tenant's raw spend with nothing naming the gap —
measured 2026-09-17 fleet-wide: $118.708744 raw against $118.184744 rolled
up, the $0.524 difference being 18 ``unregistered_tenant`` rows ($0.441435)
plus 2,750 ``health_probe`` rows ($0.082500).

⚠️ ``billing_metering_events`` HAS NO EXCLUSION COLUMN, so this covers the
COST axis only. A per-request app charge cannot be excluded this way today,
and this model must not be read as a census of everything unbilled.

⚠️ AND IT IS BOUNDED BY RAW RETENTION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON ``basis``
IS A FIELD. ``billing_cost_events`` is RANGE-partitioned on ``created_at``
with retention pruning, and was truncated 2026-09-05 — so for an older
period the honest answer is "unknown", not "none". ``basis`` is decided by
MEASUREMENT (are there any raw rows in this window at all?), never by
comparing the period against a retention setting, because the setting would
not have predicted the truncation.
InvoicePreviewExclusions.title: InvoicePreviewExclusions

InvoicePreviewResponse.description:
What this tenant's CURRENT period would bill, computed and frozen nowhere.

⛔ IT IS NOT AN INVOICE AND MUST NEVER BECOME ONE. No row is written, no
number is drawn from ``billing_invoice_counters``, no status moves. The
figures here are a REPORT over mutable inputs — markup rules, the rollup,
the licences seat count — and they will move when those move. That is the
exact property ``billing_invoices`` exists to remove, which is why a preview
carries no ``id`` and no ``invoice_number``: there is nothing here to cite.

⚠️ READ ``basis`` BEFORE ANY MONEY FIELD. Every money field is ``None`` when
``basis == "no_basis"``, and a consumer that renders ``total_usd ?? 0`` puts
a fabricated $0.00 in front of a tenant admin for a period nothing was
measured in.
InvoicePreviewResponse.title: InvoicePreviewResponse

InvoiceResponse.description:
A persisted statement, as returned by the invoice routes.

⚠️ ``excluded_unbillable_usd`` is DISCLOSED, NOT CHARGED. It is spend the
invoice gate drops (no licence reached billing) and it is deliberately not a
component of ``subtotal_usd`` or ``total_usd``. Rendering it as if it were a
line item would invert its meaning.
InvoiceResponse.title: InvoiceResponse

InvoiceSummary.description:
A persisted statement as the READ routes return it — ``InvoiceResponse``
plus the component columns a rate-card panel has to render.

⭐ A SUBCLASS, NOT A SECOND MODEL, AND NOT A WIDENING OF THE PARENT. Both
halves of that are deliberate:

* It SUBCLASSES so there is still exactly one declaration of each inherited
  field and one projector expression behind it
  (``routers.billing._invoice_summary`` builds on ``_invoice_response``).
  A parallel model repeating ``id``/``status``/``total_usd`` would be a
  second definition of the same row, free to drift from the first with
  nothing going red.
* It does NOT add these fields to ``InvoiceResponse`` itself, because that
  model is the body of ``close``/``issue``/``void`` — three routes this
  change was not asked to touch. Additive is not free on a wire contract
  that ``docs/openapi.json`` pins and that license-authz, fr-backend and
  licenses generate clients from.

⭐ THE SIX COMPONENT COLUMNS ARE HERE IN FULL, AND THAT IS THE POINT. They
are exactly ``services.invoices._TOTAL_COMPONENT_COLUMNS``, the set
``assert_total_is_the_sum_of_its_components`` gates a close on, so a panel
rendering them can show a total that its own displayed lines add up to:

    access_charge_usd + seat_fee_usd + llm_usage_usd + llm_markup_usd
      + app_request_usage_usd + app_request_markup_usd  ==  total_usd

(to within the one cent ``_TOTAL_IDENTITY_TOLERANCE_USD`` allows — the
residual is ``q(B) − B`` over the billed stream, bounded by half a cent).

⛔ DO NOT ADD ``platform_fee_usd`` OR ``excluded_unbillable_usd`` TO THAT
SUM. Both are inherited from the parent and both would INVERT if summed:
the platform fee is a surcharge already folded INSIDE
``llm_markup_usd``/``app_request_markup_usd``, and the excluded figure is
spend the statement deliberately did NOT bill. ``_TOTAL_COMPONENT_COLUMNS``
names its exclusions for exactly these reasons; read it before changing the
set here.

⚠️ THE TWO TIMESTAMPS A PANEL WANTS ARE INHERITED AND MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS.
``created_at`` is the CLOSE instant — the moment the tenant-month was frozen
— and it is always present. ``issued_at`` is when the number was minted and
is ``None`` on a draft, so "closed but not yet issued" is a real, renderable
state and not a missing field. ``voided_at`` + ``void_reason`` say a
statement was withdrawn; it keeps its number and stays readable.

⚠️ EVERY FIELD IS REQUIRED — none carries a default. ``BillingInvoice``
documents that a money column with no value "is not a zero-value invoice, it
is a generator that failed to fill one in", and ``BillingOverviewEntry
.internal_cost_exact_usd`` records what happens when a money field on a wire
model gets a default: the omission becomes invisible at the type level and
surfaces only as a confident false claim on the page. A required field makes
a forgetful producer raise.
InvoiceSummary.title: InvoiceSummary

LicenseCostBilling.description:
One license's cost block, as ``services.billing.generate_billing`` emits it.

⛔ EVERY KEY THE GENERATOR PUTS IN ``licenses[].costs`` MUST BE DECLARED HERE.
This model has no ``model_config``, so Pydantic v2 defaults to
``extra='ignore'`` and an undeclared key is dropped SILENTLY at
``routers/billing.py`` — a 200 whose body is missing the field, with nothing
in the logs. That is the same failure ``InvoiceDocument`` records below, and
it had already happened here: the INCURRED half of every figure was declared
and the BILLED half was not, so ``billed_cost_usd``, ``llm_billed_usd``,
``app_request_billed_usd``, ``markup_pct`` and ``billed_by_provider`` — the
entire billed/markup axis, i.e. what the tenant is actually CHARGED — were
computed on every request and discarded on the way out. A caller could read
what the spend cost us and never what it cost them.

``tests/test_invoice_itemisation_is_self_consistent.py`` derives the expected
key set from the generator's own output rather than a hardcoded list, so the
next field added to the generator and forgotten here reds rather than
vanishes.
LicenseCostBilling.title: LicenseCostBilling

LicenseUsageBilling.description:
One license's usage block, as ``services.billing.generate_billing`` emits it.

⛔ Same ``extra='ignore'`` drop as ``LicenseCostBilling`` below — see that
docstring. Measured against the generator's ``licenses[].usage`` dict:
``denied_count`` and ``budget_denied_count`` were emitted on every request
and discarded on the way out, so the REFUSAL axis of a licence's month never
reached the wire while the admitted-request count did. The two are not
interchangeable and neither is derivable from the other: ``denied_count`` is
every refusal (``metering_daily.denied``) and ``budget_denied_count`` is the
subset refused specifically for want of token budget, which is the one an
operator can fix by raising a budget.
LicenseUsageBilling.title: LicenseUsageBilling

One row in the system-wide per-tenant breakdown.

`incurred_cost_usd` is raw provider/internal cost (no markup, no allowance
netting). `effective_incurred_cost_usd` is that cost AFTER the tenant's
included-usage allowance has been consumed -- the base markup is actually
applied to. `billed_cost_usd` is what the tenant is charged.

self-checking:

raw cost, a different quantity that goes NEGATIVE whenever an allowance is
granted, and this field's fallback arm publishes a configured rate. The
reader can still compute realised uplift from the two cost columns.

post.description:
Permanently drop dead-letter entries that no replay can ever drain.

The escape hatch for the third state the runbook has no move for: an entry
that is neither fixable nor replayable, because the malformed condition is
IN the stored payload. ``nil_tenant_id`` is the case — ``replay_dlq``
re-injects the stored fields, ``validate_cost_event`` re-rejects them
identically, and the entry re-quarantines forever while
BillingCostDeadLetterBacklog fires.

``confirm`` defaults to **false** — a plain call is a DRY RUN reporting what
would be discarded, and deletes nothing. An entry is only ever eligible when
it is BOTH ``cost_usd == 0`` AND unattributable (absent or nil tenant);
anything else is refused and counted, never deleted. See
:func:`services.dlq_ops.discard_dlq` for the deletion principle this excepts
and why these entries are the exception.

One audit row per invocation, dry runs included.

tenant is nil or blank are accepted; the target must be a registered,
non-nil tenant (400 otherwise). The rewritten event goes through replay's
own marker claim, validation and atomic re-inject, so it is billed at most
once, and a Postgres receipt is committed before the entry is XDELed.

``confirm`` defaults to **false** — a plain call is a DRY RUN. Gated on
``require_admin`` (license-admin), NOT ``require_pricing_admin``: this
decides which customer is charged, and the ``billing-internal`` service
account must not be able to do that (same reasoning as
``require_pricing_writer``). One audit row per invocation, dry runs included.

and one bad entry never aborts the batch. Exactly one audit row per

data. Already-priced events are never touched, so re-running is a no-op.

get.description: Recent audit-log rows, newest-first. License-admin only.

One tenant's statements, newest period first.

⛔ THE ``tenant_id`` PREDICATE IS THE ISOLATION, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL.
``require_service_caller`` proves the caller is an internal service; it says
NOTHING about which tenant they may read, because an internal SA token
legitimately spans the estate. Every row returned here is therefore selected
by an explicit ``WHERE tenant_id =`` rather than filtered afterwards — a
post-filter is one forgotten ``continue`` away from leaking another
customer's platform fee and margin. ``enforce_tenant_isolation`` below is the
second, independent gate for the proxying case.

⭐ VOIDED AND DRAFT STATEMENTS ARE INCLUDED, DELIBERATELY. ``void`` is a
terminal status that KEEPS its invoice number and stays readable — that is
what lets a reader see a statement was superseded rather than destroyed (see
``void_billing_invoice``) — and hiding it here would make a re-closed period
look like it had only ever been billed once. ``status`` discriminates; the
caller filters if it wants to.

⚠️ THE SECOND ORDERING KEY IS NOT DECORATION. ``ix_billing_invoices_tenant_
period`` is ``(tenant_id, period_start DESC)``, which is the index this scan
wants, but ``period_start`` is NOT unique per tenant: voiding a statement
drops it out of ``ux_billing_invoices_open_period`` precisely so the period
can be closed AGAIN, so a re-billed month holds two or more rows sharing
every ordering column. Without ``created_at DESC`` the planner is free to
return them in either order, and a panel showing "the latest invoice for
September" would show the VOIDED one on some page loads and the live one on
others, non-deterministically. ``id`` breaks the residual tie so the order is
total.

post.description:
Freeze one tenant-month into a persisted statement.

IDEMPOTENT, and deliberately 200 rather than 201 or 409: a repeat call
returns the existing live invoice for the period unchanged and does NOT
recompute. Recomputing would produce a different answer whenever a markup
rule moved in between, which is the exact failure this object exists to
prevent.

Refuses rather than degrades in five cases. A period whose ``total_usd`` is
not the sum of the component columns that explain it is an
InvoiceMoneyImbalanceError -> 409: the statement does not add up, and the row
is immutable and drawn from a gapless series once written, so there is no
edit afterwards. A period containing a day with
no rollup rows at all is a BucketGapError -> 409: the source is absent for
that date, so any total is short by an unknown amount and a statement that
cannot say so is worse than no statement. A period with billable requests on
a service_key that has no billing_app_cost_rates row is an
UnpricedServiceKeyError -> ALSO 409, and for the same reason: that app line
would be invoiced at a fabricated $0.00, indistinguishable on the statement
from a deliberately free service, on an invoice number that is gapless and
irreversible. A period holding cost events that no provider_pricing row could
price (billing_cost_daily.unpriced_event_count > 0) is an
UnpricedProviderCostError -> ALSO 409: the rollup's coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0)
has already turned that unknown spend into a hard $0.000000, so closing would
freeze "free" where the truth is "unknown" — understating internal cost and
overstating margin. ⚠️ It is a DISTINCT error from UnpricedServiceKeyError and
is mapped separately on purpose: the remedy is a row in provider_pricing, not
in billing_app_cost_rates, and an operator handed one message for the other
edits the wrong table. A period that is not one calendar month is an
InvoicePeriodError -> 422 rather than being widened to the month containing
it.

get.description:
What this period WOULD bill, computed now and frozen nowhere.

⛔ IT CLOSES NOTHING AND CONSUMES NO INVOICE NUMBER. ``generate_billing`` is
a pure read — SELECTs plus the licences lookups — and this handler adds three
more SELECTs and no write. In particular it never reaches
``services.invoices.issue``, so ``billing_invoice_counters.next_seq`` does
not move: a caller may preview the same period a thousand times and the
gapless series is untouched. There is no ``session.commit()`` below on
purpose; ``get_session`` never commits and the session's exit rolls back, so
the read path leaves nothing behind even if something upstream dirtied the
identity map.

⭐ THE SEAT COUNT IS THE PERIOD'S, NOT ``now()``'s — AND ``generate_billing``
ALREADY GUARANTEES THAT, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROUTE REUSES IT RATHER THAN
REBUILDING A PREVIEW. Its per-seat block resolves every term through
``_resolve_seat_count(tenant_id, settings, as_of=bill_ts, **scope)`` where
``bill_ts`` is the LAST INSTANT OF THE BILLED MONTH, and ``scope`` comes from
``services.seats.seat_scope_for_charge``. That gives two bases, both
period-anchored and neither of them a wall-clock count:

* a ``seat:<app>`` term (CommonPractice's shape, written by
  ``PUT /commercial-terms``) → ``seat_basis = "active_during_period"``: that
  one app's seats held at ANY instant in ``[period_start, period_end)``,
  counted as ``human_subjects`` — DISTINCT PEOPLE, not licence rows, so an
  employee revoked and re-licensed inside the month is one seat and a
  service-realm licence is none;
* an unpinned term (the legacy ``__seat__``, or a NULL ``service_key``) →
  ``seat_basis = "active_licences"``, counted ``as_of`` the last instant of
  the period, also as ``human_subjects`` (#265): ``service`` and
  ``cp-tenant`` subjects are not seats.

⚠️ THE ONE HONEST RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. For a CURRENT period
the unpinned basis' ``as_of`` is in the FUTURE, and licences resolves a
future instant against today's rows — so mid-month that count is effectively
the live one. That is not a defect being papered over: end-of-month seats are
genuinely unknowable on the 12th, and ``seat_basis`` is on the response so a
reader can see WHICH basis produced the number instead of assuming. The
period-scoped basis has no such residual: it counts the window that has
actually elapsed. ⛔ Do not "fix" this by substituting ``as_of=now()`` — that
would also change the answer for a CLOSED period, which is the one case
``as_of`` exists to get right.

⚠️ ``seat_basis = "unavailable"`` is a THIRD outcome and does not mean zero
seats: it means licences could not be asked, and the report path fails SOFT
with a $0.00 seat line precisely so a dashboard survives a licences outage.
``close_period`` refuses to freeze that state instead. A consumer that
renders the seat line without reading ``seat_basis`` will show $0.00 for a
paying tenant during an outage.

⛔ AND A MISSING BASIS IS NOT A ZERO BILL. See ``basis`` /
``InvoicePreviewResponse``: when nothing underlies the period every money
field is ``None``, never 0.00.

⛔ A FOREIGN INVOICE IS **404**, NOT 403, AND THE TENANT IS IN THE ``WHERE``
CLAUSE RATHER THAN IN AN ``if`` AFTER THE FETCH. Both halves matter:

* 403 would be an ORACLE. "Forbidden" says the id EXISTS and belongs to
  someone else; 404 says only "not yours, here". Invoice ids are uuid4, so
  enumeration is not the threat — a caller holding a leaked id learning it is
  live is. The two refusals are indistinguishable to a legitimate caller and
  quite different to an illegitimate one.
* Filtering in SQL means the row for another tenant is never loaded into this
  process at all, so no later edit to this handler — a log line, an error
  message, a debug dump — can leak a field off it. A post-fetch check is one
  forgotten ``raise`` away from returning the row it just rejected.

⚠️ REGISTRATION ORDER: this route MUST stay below ``/invoices/preview``. See
the block comment above ``_invoice_summary``.

post.description:
Buy PREPAID CREDIT and INVOICE it -- once per ``idempotency_key``.

One transaction: a ``topup`` credit entry on the tenant's credit ledger (USD
at the FX rate effective now); a ``cadence='one_time'`` access charge
(service_key ``topup:<topup_id>``) that the invoice generator itemises in
this month; an audit row. Later statements net their LLM usage against the
credit and bill only usage beyond it. The money-budget cap is NOT touched.
A replay with the same key and body returns the original top-up with
``replayed: true`` and writes nothing.

put.description:
Set the tenant's whole-unit budget (idempotent) and flip budget_unit='money'.

A replay with the same body changes nothing and returns the same
``budget_id``; a new amount updates the ONE active row in place.
``currency`` creates the budget in that currency; a different currency than

Pre-flight token reservation against the tenant's active budget pool.

license-authz calls this on the request hot path. Atomically (via Redis
Lua) checks ``consumed + reserved + estimated <= sum(budget_tokens)`` and
decrements a short-TTL ``reserved`` counter on success. Actual cost is
debited post-fact via the cost-event flush (existing path); the
``reserved`` counter auto-expires so over-estimates self-correct.

Status codes:
  * 200 — reservation granted.
  * 429 — denied (over budget OR no active budget). Response body still
    carries the cap/consumed/remaining numbers so the caller can decide
    whether to retry with a smaller estimate or 402 the user.

Zero the current-period consumption of every ACTIVE budget a tenant holds.

⛔ INTERNAL BY CONSTRUCTION — ``require_internal`` (a verified Keycloak
SERVICE-ACCOUNT token), never ``require_tenant``. A licence token is held
by every member of a tenant, and ext_authz turns one into an ``X-Tenant-Id``
header, so ``require_tenant`` + tenant isolation would let a CUSTOMER zero
their own consumption — free money. This route therefore reads no tenant
header at all and pairs with no isolation check: with ``require_internal``
there is nothing to isolate against, and a guard that can never fire is
worse than none. Same gate as the two other budget writes in this file
(``create_token_budget`` / ``topup_tenant_budget``).

Scope is the SAME set the status endpoint reports
(``_select_active_budgets(..., lock=False)``, i.e. active AND inside its
current window — see ``check_budget_aggregate``): the operator resets what
they just looked at, and a row the gate cannot spend against (expired, or
not started yet) is not part of that view.

empty 200, which would tell a caller who mistyped the tenant that their

get.description:
Self-service budget status — uses the caller's active X-Tenant-Id.

UI already knows it from the active workspace). 400 if the tenant
header is missing — without it there's no budget to look up.

This route deliberately does NOT depend on ``require_tenant`` like its
siblings, for two reasons that are specific to ``/me``:

* ``require_tenant`` treats an ABSENT header as "maybe an admin JWT" and
  falls through to ``verify_admin_token``, which answers **401** ("Tenant
  context required"). This route's contract is a **400**: the caller is
  authenticated, they just have no active workspace selected, and telling
  them to re-authenticate cannot help.
* The admin-JWT branch resolves the caller's own ``sub``. A Keycloak
  service-account ``sub`` is a uuid, so it resolves cleanly and ``/me``
  would silently answer for "the tenant whose id happens to equal this
  service account" — the ``__admin__`` pseudo-tenant defect re-entering by
  another door. On ``/me`` there is no such thing as an admin caller: "me"
  IS the header.

So the header is read directly, but resolved through the SAME resolver the
header path uses, ONCE, at the top — a registered tenant name has to reach
``check_budget_aggregate`` as a uuid or Postgres answers with a DataError.

⚠️ OPERATOR-TRIGGERED ONLY. This is a **manual reconcile of last resort**,
not a background job. Nothing calls it on a timer: there is no scheduler, no
CronJob, no watcher loop, and no startup hook anywhere in this service that
invokes it. It runs if and only if a human (or a runbook step) POSTs to it.

Do not read this route's existence as "budgets track licences
automatically". They do not. Between two manual invocations, a plan change
upstream — a new licence, a changed ``token_budget_monthly``, a
downgrade-to-0, a deactivation that should orphan a budget — is simply not
reflected here. The steady-state writer is licence issuance itself; this
endpoint exists to repair the drift that accumulates when that path missed
something.

Consequently a failure here is silent by default. Treat a response with a
non-null ``error`` (or zero counts where rows were expected) as an incident,
not as a no-op: nothing else will notice. The same goes for a non-zero
``skipped_count``: those licences were deliberately passed over because they
name no resolvable tenant, and no later run will fix them by itself.

put.description:
Set a tenant's ENTIRE commercial rate card in one database transaction.

Writes, in this order and under one commit:

1. `tenant_config.billing_mode` — the outer gate over every markup resolution.
2. a tenant-wide `cadence='monthly'` access charge — the flat platform fee,
   with `included_cost_usd` left NULL so usage bills ON TOP of it rather than
   the first N dollars being silently free.
3. a `cadence='per_seat'` access charge on `seat:<seat_app_key>` — a RATE,
   multiplied by that product's seat count at bill time.
4. a `byo=True` markup rule scoped to `markup_service_key`.

⭐ IDEMPOTENT ON VALUE, NOT ON EXISTENCE, and the distinction is the whole
reason this is safe to retry. `upsert_access_charge` and `upsert_markup_rule`
CLOSE the prior open row and open a new one — that is what makes the history
auditable, and it is also what makes a naive "a PUT always writes" version
catastrophic: every provisioning retry would end the current period and start
a fresh one, so a tenant would appear re-priced on whatever schedule the saga
happened to retry on, and the effective-dated history the two stores exist to
keep would be shredded into noise. So each term is compared to the OPEN row
first and rewritten only when the requested value actually differs. A replay
with the same body writes nothing, commits nothing, and returns
`changed: []`.

⚠️ AND `changed` IS THE OBSERVABLE THAT MAKES THAT CHECKABLE. Without it a
caller cannot tell "the terms already said this" from "I just re-dated four
periods", which are the two outcomes whose difference matters.

⛔ THE LEGACY `__seat__` ROW IS CLOSED WHEN THIS WRITES `seat:<app>`. They are
DIFFERENT open slots under `ix_accesscharge_open`, and
`services.billing.generate_billing` sums EVERY `cadence='per_seat'` row it
finds — so leaving both open bills the tenant twice for seats, silently, on a
line that looks correct in isolation. A tenant previously put on the standard
card by `POST /tenants/{id}/terms` is exactly the tenant this endpoint is
called on next, so this is the common path, not an edge case.

`require_pricing_writer` — is DELIBERATE, not an oversight: reading terms

customer / license-authz-forwarded tenant context, as opposed to an admin

to anyone) no longer exists. A wrongful 404 here would become a wrongful
customer-facing 402 the instant license-authz runs with
``METERING_FAIL_OPEN=false`` (its ``check`` turns a 4xx into a deny), so the

row's owner.

Readiness probe — 503 when a FATAL dependency is down.

Two separate lessons are encoded here; do not collapse them.

**The status code has to move.** This used to return a bare
ReadinessResponse, which FastAPI serialises at the decorator's status code
(200) for *every* outcome, ready or not. The Deployment wires this path as
an httpGet readinessProbe, and an httpGet probe reads only the status code
— never the body. So a billing pod that could not reach Postgres still
reported Ready and stayed in the Service's endpoint rotation indefinitely,
taking revenue-path traffic it could not serve. That part stands.

**But not every dependency is fatal, and Redis is not** (fr#947/#978,
2026-09-06). fr and kag served zero endpoints for 2h45m because their
readiness awaited Redis and 503'd on it: a control-plane blip wedged the
Redis client in every replica at once, `/health/live` stayed 200 so
kubelet restarted nothing, and a human had to notice. Redis was healthy
the whole time — a fresh PING from inside a wedged container answered in
4-8ms.

Readiness expresses a **per-pod** condition: "route to me, not to my
siblings". A dependency that every replica shares cannot express that. It
turns readiness into a correlated fleet-wide kill switch with nothing left
to route to. `billing-service` runs `replicas: 2` against a
**single-replica** Redis Deployment, so gating readiness on Redis made a
1-replica SPOF able to empty the endpoints of the entire revenue path.

And this service is already designed to run without Redis. See
`routers/quota.py`'s `get_redis()  # may be None - the durable write below
still proceeds`, the `redis_conn is None` branch in every service module,
and `lifespan`'s own note about "a Redis-less pod". Readiness treating
Redis as fatal contradicted the code it gates.

So: **Postgres stays fatal** — without it this service cannot read or
write anything and a 503 correctly sheds traffic to a sibling that can.
**Redis degrades instead**: `status` becomes `degraded`, `redis` still
reads `disconnected`, the dependency is named in `degraded[]`, and a WARN
is logged every probe. The signal is preserved and alertable; only the
fatality is dropped. Deleting the check would have been the wrong fix.

Recovery is not left to luck either: `check_redis()` supervises the client
and rebuilds it once it has demonstrably stopped recovering (see
`redis_client`). Staying Ready through a Redis fault is what keeps this
probe ticking so that repair can run.
